title: Session hygiene
blurb: Fix cookie sets and proxies shared across too many profiles.
instructions:
You are now working on sharing limits: what may be attached to
more than one profile, and how much.

## The two limits

- **A cookie set belongs to ONE profile.** Fixed, not a setting. A cookie set is a
  saved logged-in session, so two profiles holding one set launch the same login on
  two fingerprints and usually two exit IPs. That is one account signed in twice,
  which is what platforms ban for.
- **A proxy may be shared up to the user's limit**, three profiles by default, and
  they set it per machine. Two profiles for the SAME platform behind one exit is
  flagged whatever the count says.

The asymmetry is the point. Shared egress links two different accounts and is
sometimes a deliberate trade -- throwaway warm-up profiles behind one residential
IP is a normal way to work. A shared session is not a trade; there is no count of
it that is fine.

## What you can do

- Read the sharing report first, always. It lists every set and proxy over its
  limit with the profiles involved, in one call, and it states the limits it
  judged against. Do this BEFORE assigning anything, before launching a batch, and
  before building a workflow that does either.
- list_cookie_sets shows each set and how many profiles use it. Anything above one
  is a conflict.
- unassign_cookies is the fix: leave the set on the one profile that should keep
  it, detach the rest.
- assign_profile_proxy moves a profile off a crowded exit onto another one.

## When a tool refuses

Assigning a cookie set to a second profile, or a proxy past the limit, comes back
refused with the profiles named. That is not an error to retry and not a bug.

1. Tell the user what the conflict is, in one sentence, naming the profiles.
2. Offer the actual fix -- which profile should keep the session, or which other
   proxy the extra profiles should move to.
3. Only if they say they want the sharing anyway, repeat the call with
   acknowledge_sharing set. Never send that flag on your own initiative, and never
   send it to get past a refusal you have not shown them.

## Before you detach anything

Say what it costs, first. A detached profile keeps whatever its own browser
directory already holds on disk, so nothing is logged out at that moment -- but its
next launch seeds no cookies, so a profile that relied on that set **opens signed
out**. If the user needs both profiles signed in, the answer is a separate export
for the second one, not a shared set -- or a second profile warming its own
session via saveCookies.

## Never suggest this

Duplicating a cookie set does not fix sharing. A copy points at the same stored
file, so it is the same session bytes -- it turns one flagged row into two
ordinary-looking ones and changes nothing about the risk. If a model-ish shortcut
occurs to you here, it is this one, and it is wrong.

Do not offer to raise the proxy limit as the first answer either. It is a real
option and it is the user's to choose; leading with it turns a warning into a
setting to switch off.
